item.text: {"kind":"tools","payload_json":"{\"calls\":[{\"name\":\"artifact.write_text\",\"arguments\":{\"path\":\"hypothesis_evidence_map.json\",\"text\":\"{\\n  \\\"task_id\\\": \\\"dev-exp-001\\\",\\n  \\\"method_fidelity\\\": {\\n    \\\"implementation\\\": \\\"coupled_estimator.py\\\",\\n    \\\"configs\\\": \\\"experiment_configs.json\\\",\\n    \\\"analysis_code\\\": \\\"run_experiments.py\\\",\\n    \\\"statement\\\": \\\"The implementation uses zero initialization, positive constant step sizes, unnormalized gradient sums, and simultaneous updates from old theta and old beta. Cached B=Z.T@Z, C=Z.T@X, and d=Z.T@Y products are algebraically equivalent to the specified updates; exact least-squares solutions are used only as comparators and diagnostics.\\\"\\n  },\\n  \\\"hypotheses\\\": [\\n    {\\n      \\\"hypothesis_id\\\": \\\"H1\\\",\\n      \\\"experiment_ids\\\": [\\n        \\\"All 80 stable-family experiment IDs in run_outputs.json: 20 datasets crossed with S_balanced, S_alpha_slow, S_eta_slow, and S_near_boundary\\\"\\n      ],\\n      \\\"artifact_references\\\": [\\n        \\\"coupled_estimator.py\\\",\\n        \\\"experiment_configs.json\\\",\\n        \\\"run_experiments.py\\\",\\n        \\\"run_outputs.json\\\",\\n        \\\"diagnostics.csv\\\",\\n        \\\"analysis_summary.json\\\"\\n      ],\\n      \\\"short_conclusion\\\": \\\"Supported for the tested identified Gaussian samples, with qualifications on finite horizons and rate estimation. All 80 within-region runs completed 10,000 iterations; 78/80 had final relative beta error below 1e-8 versus sample 2SLS. Scenario median final beta errors were 1.75e-15 (balanced), 8.78e-15 (alpha-slow), 3.38e-15 (eta-slow), and 2.89e-15 (near-boundary). The two runs not below 1e-8 were finite-horizon slow cases: default seed 6 under alpha-slow had 1.43e-5 error with Lambda=0.998913 and cond(A)=91.98, while near-square seed 102 under eta-slow had 1.39e-8 beta error and 1.10e-6 theta error with Lambda=0.998861 and cond(B)=87.79. Where a late log-linear fit remained above the numerical floor, alpha-slow supplied 12 supported fits whose median fitted factor was 0.994558, close to its median Lambda 0.993716; individual high-quality examples in diagnostics.csv likewise closely track Lambda. Most faster runs reached floating-point floors before the predeclared fit window, so their late-rate fits are explicitly unsupported rather than treated as evidence against geometric convergence.\\\",\\n      \\\"uncertainty\\\": \\\"This is finite-sample, finite-seed numerical evidence from 20 datasets across five regimes. Only 17/80 predeclared late-window fits were supported because most traces reached approximately 1e-15 precision before the fitting window. A supported flag alone is not sufficient: the isolated balanced and near-boundary fits at the numerical floor are not interpreted as rate evidence. Conditioning ranged from 5.23 to 91.98 for A and 1.87 to 87.79 for B, explaining substantial transient and horizon variation.\\\",\\n      \\\"limitations_and_unperformed_work\\\": [\\n        \\\"No general convergence theorem is claimed.\\\",\\n        \\\"The experiment does not establish population consistency, causal identification beyond the supplied sample regime, or any Transformer capability.\\\",\\n        \\\"The target is sample 2SLS; truth-error fields are descriptive comparators and were not used for fitting or initialization.\\\",\\n        \\\"The final design used 20 predeclared datasets and a 10,000-iteration stable horizon after two documented 120-second timeouts of larger designs; this deviation is recorded in experiment_configs.json.\\\",\\n        \\\"No additional precision arithmetic or longer follow-up was performed for the two slow finite-horizon cases.\\\"\\n      ]\\n    },\\n    {\\n      \\\"hypothesis_id\\\": \\\"H2\\\",\\n      \\\"experiment_ids\\\": [\\n        \\\"All 80 stable-family and 60 outside-family experiment IDs in run_outputs.json\\\"\\n      ],\\n      \\\"artifact_references\\\": [\\n        \\\"experiment_configs.json\\\",\\n        \\\"run_experiments.py\\\",\\n        \\\"run_outputs.json\\\",\\n        \\\"diagnostics.csv\\\",\\n        \\\"analysis_summary.json\\\"\\n      ],\\n      \\\"short_conclusion\\\": \\\"Supported for the tested step-size contrasts. Reducing alpha to 5% of its upper bound made gamma the Lambda bottleneck in 18/20 datasets and produced conspicuously larger errors at iteration 200; reducing eta similarly made kappa the bottleneck in 18/20 datasets, with especially slow theta-driven behavior in the ill-conditioned near-square regime. The paired iteration-200 records show that balanced and 95%-of-boundary settings were generally much farther along than the deliberately slowed block, although coupled transients prevent a universal ordering. Outside the candidate region, all tested settings were unstable over the chosen horizons: alpha at 101% completed 2,000 iterations but had enormous final beta relative errors (median 2.00e15, range 2.43e13 to 3.28e16), while eta at 101% and both steps at 125% crossed the 1e100 divergence threshold in all 20 datasets. This demonstrates that completion status alone is not convergence and that Lambda correctly identifies the unstable block in these settings.\\\",\\n      \\\"uncertainty\\\": \\\"Bottleneck counts and iteration-200 comparisons are paired within each generated dataset, avoiding cross-seed confounding, but they cover only four within-region and three outside-region step choices. Lambda is an asymptotic block diagnostic and does not encode all nonlinear coupled transients. Outside-region observations are limited to 20 datasets and horizons of at most 2,000 iterations.\\\",\\n      \\\"limitations_and_unperformed_work\\\": [\\n        \\\"No claim is made that every setting outside the candidate region must diverge.\\\",\\n        \\\"No dense boundary sweep was performed, so the experiments do not locate a sharp empirical stability frontier.\\\",\\n        \\\"The 1e100 threshold is an operational divergence safeguard, not a mathematical definition of divergence.\\\",\\n        \\\"The near-boundary within-region scenario was fast for these spectra because using 95% of the upper bound gives extreme-eigenvalue factors near 0.9; its label refers to the step bound, not necessarily slow convergence.\\\"\\n      ]\\n    }\\n  ]\\n}\\n\"}}]}"}
